bss.topic: Ritmos da natureza: dia e noite, temperatura e umidade

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quando o Sol está no céu e tudo fica claro, é…
questions.hint: Pense em quando você vai para a escola.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que costumamos ver no céu à noite?
questions.hint: Lembre do céu na hora de dormir.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: De manhã, o Sol aparece de que lado do céu?
questions.hint: É o lado que chamamos de nascente.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: No fim da tarde, o Sol se põe de que lado do céu?
questions.hint: É o lado contrário ao de onde o Sol nasce.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que existe o dia e a noite?
options: Porque a Terra gira em torno de si mesma
Porque o Sol se apaga à noite
Porque as nuvens escondem o Sol
questions.answer: Porque a Terra gira em torno de si mesma
questions.hint: O Sol não se apaga: quem se mexe é o nosso planeta.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quantas horas, mais ou menos, a Terra leva para dar uma volta completa em torno de si mesma?
questions.hint: É o tempo de um dia inteiro, juntando o dia e a noite.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual instrumento mede a temperatura?
questions.hint: É o mesmo tipo de instrumento usado quando temos febre.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Responda com uma palavra: num dia muito quente, a temperatura está alta ou baixa?
questions.hint: Quanto mais calor, maior o número no termômetro.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em geral, em que parte do dia faz mais calor?
options: Perto do meio-dia e no começo da tarde
questions.answer: Perto do meio-dia e no começo da tarde
questions.hint: Pense em quando o Sol está mais alto.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que é a umidade do ar?
options: A quantidade de água que existe no ar
questions.answer: A quantidade de água que existe no ar
questions.hint: A água pode estar no ar sem a gente ver.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em qual destes dias a umidade do ar costuma estar mais alta?
options: Num dia muito seco e sem nuvens
Num dia de muito vento seco
questions.hint: Pense em quando há mais água por perto.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quando o ar está muito seco, o que é bom fazer?
options: Correr no sol forte do meio-dia
questions.hint: Nosso corpo também precisa de água.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Perto do meio-dia, como costuma ficar a nossa sombra?
questions.hint: Nessa hora o Sol está bem alto, em cima da gente.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: No fim da tarde, com o Sol baixinho, como fica a nossa sombra?
questions.hint: Compare com a sombra do meio-dia.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: De manhã o termômetro marcou 18 graus. À tarde marcou 25 graus. Quantos graus a temperatura subiu?
questions.hint: Conte de 18 até 25.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Conte uma coisa que você faz de dia e uma que você faz de noite. Por que elas combinam com esse horário?
questions.hint: Pense na luz do Sol e no descanso.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: When we join our handwriting, what does a joining stroke do?
options: It links one letter to the next
questions.answer: It links one letter to the next
questions.hint: Think about what 'join' means.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these letters is a tall letter with an ascender?
questions.hint: Which letter reaches up higher than the others?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these letters has a descender (a tail that goes below the line)?
questions.hint: Look for the letter that hangs down.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: A diagonal join usually starts from which part of the first letter?
questions.hint: Picture the stroke going up like a little slope.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In the word 'in', how does the join from i to n go?
options: Diagonally up from the bottom of i
Straight across from the top of i
Down from the dot of i
questions.answer: Diagonally up from the bottom of i
questions.hint: The i finishes at the bottom, then you go up to start n.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which pair uses a diagonal join up to a tall letter?
questions.hint: Find the pair where the second letter has an ascender.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word starts with a diagonal join to a short letter?
questions.hint: Short letters have no ascender.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Small letters like a, c, e, m and n should be…
options: as tall as l and h
questions.hint: Neat writing looks even.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Tall letters like l, h and k should be…
options: taller than small letters like a and n
the same height as a and n
questions.answer: taller than small letters like a and n
questions.hint: Think about the ascender reaching up.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Where should all your letters sit?
questions.hint: The line is like the floor for your letters.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why do we keep our letters a consistent size?
options: So our writing is easy to read
questions.answer: So our writing is easy to read
questions.hint: Think about the person reading your work.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What do we call the part of a tall letter that goes up above the small letters?
questions.hint: It 'ascends', which means goes up.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What do we call the tail of a letter that goes below the line, like in g or y?
questions.hint: It 'descends', which means goes down.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: How many tall letters with ascenders are in the word 'little'?
questions.hint: Look for letters that reach up higher than i and e.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: How many letters with descenders are in the word 'puppy'?
questions.hint: Count every letter whose tail goes below the line.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write the word 'hill' in joined handwriting. Which letters must you make tall, and how do the letters join?
questions.hint: Look at each letter and think about its height.

questions.q: Where does Lila go to tell the sky the secret?
questions.hint: She needs to be high up, close to the sky.

questions.subject: en_read

questions.hint: The secret is about making the sky cry.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What falls from the sky at the end of the story? (one word)
questions.hint: It is what the village needed.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: When there is no rain for a very long time, we call it a…
questions.hint: It is the opposite of too much water.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why is rain so important for Lila's village?
options: Plants can grow and people have water
questions.answer: Plants can grow and people have water
questions.hint: What do crops and people need to live?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: The setting of a story is…
questions.hint: Think about the place in the story.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which words best describe the weather in Lila's village at the start?
questions.hint: Remember the problem the village had.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: How do you think the people in the village feel when the rain comes?
questions.hint: They waited a long time for it.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which is true about both Brazil and Kenya?
options: Both have places where it can be very hot
Both are covered in ice all year
questions.answer: Both have places where it can be very hot
questions.hint: Think about the weather in each country.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which sentence compares Lila's village with a big Brazilian city like São Paulo?
options: Lila's village is small and dusty, but São Paulo has many tall buildings
Both are tiny villages with no roads
São Paulo is in Kenya too
questions.answer: Lila's village is small and dusty, but São Paulo has many tall buildings
questions.hint: A comparison shows how two places are alike or different.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Lila was brave to climb up and talk to the sky. Why do you think she wanted to help her village?
questions.hint: Think about her family and friends.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Think about a rainy day where you live. How is it different from the dry days in Lila's village?
questions.hint: Think about what you see, hear and feel.

questions.q: Which word is spelt correctly?

questions.subject: en_spell

questions.hint: The baby is doing it right now.

questions.subject: en_spell

questions.hint: With -ed the y changes; with -ing it stays.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Add -ing to "reply". Write the whole word.

questions.subject: en_spell

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Why do we keep the y in "trying"?
options: Because "triing" would have two i's together
questions.answer: Because "triing" would have two i's together
questions.hint: Look at what happens if you change y to i and add -ing.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 4 misspelled words.
questions.answer: frieing → frying; crieing → crying; hurriing → hurrying; carriing → carrying
questions.hint: Look at words ending in -ing.
questions.text: Mum was frieing pancakes in the kitchen. My little brother was crieing because he was hungry. I was hurriing to set the table and carriing the plates. Dad was copying a funny joke to tell us. Soon we were all eating and laughing together.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Pick the correct spelling of "carry" + -ing.
questions.hint: Keep the y from "carry".

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Pick the correct spelling of "worry" + -ing.
questions.hint: Do not change the y.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Pick the correct spelling of "study" + -ing.
questions.hint: Keep every letter of "study".
